niche.habitat: Coastal islet, sea arches, tidal causeways, and the giant tree spring.
niche.diet: Herbivore: high-canopy foliage, salt spray, mineral licks, and floating carcasses.
niche.active: Diurnal, slow-paced; active during low tide and clear days.

body: Colossal browser with a long neck that reaches the giant tree's canopy and a mass that anchors it against the island's 1.6× wind force. Its slow, duet-sway gait conserves energy in dense air, while its colossal stomping gait communicates across the islet and triggers tidal resonance awareness.

links: No land predator on the islet, so bulk costs nothing in escape speed
Cold upwelling feeds plankton-rich shallows, so a giant can graze the surf all year
1.6 bar air with pO2 0.34 bar funds a huge aerobic gut
At 1.05 g, wide feet and a slow gait beat running

skill.effect: Wades 1.2 m deep for 20 s behind a 3 m bow wave; leaves the islet only at spring low, when the 3.2 m shelf tide uncovers the causeway.

chains.weakness: Deep water and high tide: lure it onto the flat as the tide turns and it is cut off for a full 14.9 d cycle, turning its back on you.
observe: huge prints in the tidal flat

journal.en: The islet kept it big and slow.

plausibility.summary: State explicitly a giant-tortoise-grade resting metabolism and a mixed diet (intertidal algae mats + wrack + high canopy); surf alone rarely sustains multi-ton mass year-round. Optionally note Coloso is the last or near-last giant on the islet, not proof that gigantism evolved with zero predation pressure everywhere.
fixes: State explicitly a giant-tortoise-grade resting metabolism and a mixed diet (intertidal algae mats + wrack + high canopy); surf alone rarely sustains multi-ton mass year-round. Optionally note Coloso is the last or near-last giant on the islet, not proof that gigantism evolved with zero predation pressure everywhere.

analogues.organism: Galápagos giant tortoise (Chelonoidis niger) — insular gigantism with abundant low-quality browse and reduced predation (MacArthur & Wilson 1967, island biogeography, from memory, unverified); hippopotamus — bulk wading in shallow water.
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

links: Islet browse is sparse and goes bare each dry season
Kelp holdfasts and stripped canopy sit at 4 m, above every other grazer
Reach was cheaper than height: the neck grew, the legs stayed short against winter gales

skill.effect: Eats leaves or fruit up to 4 m without lowering its guard; fruit gifts offered at head height count +15 instead of +8.

chains.weakness: Blind under its own chin: lure it beneath a rock arch and strike the neck from the far side; it cannot turn its head fast at close range.

journal.en: It eats what nothing else can reach.

plausibility.summary: Drop "kelp holdfasts at 4 m" (holdfasts are benthic). Use storm-pruned coastal trees, lianas, and stacked intertidal wrack / canopy leftovers in a ~4 m band; short legs are wind-loading tradeoff on the islet (F19), accepting slower travel on steep dyke rock.
fixes: Drop "kelp holdfasts at 4 m" (holdfasts are benthic). Use storm-pruned coastal trees, lianas, and stacked intertidal wrack / canopy leftovers in a ~4 m band; short legs are wind-loading tradeoff on the islet (F19), accepting slower travel on steep dyke rock.

analogues.organism: Giraffe (Giraffa camelopardalis) — height/reach competition for browse; extinct moa (Dinornis spp.) — large island browser with neck reach (from memory, unverified).
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

links: A retained mainland pair-bond ritual (F27) persists in a solitary adult, causing heterospecific redirection to any large, slow mimic
Dense air (F4) and high O2 (F5) allow low-frequency body rumbles to travel far on foggy dawns (F8), sustaining an obligate 0.5 Hz sway without metabolic fatigue
High drag (F4) and 1.05 g (F2) enforce slow metabolic pacing, making the visual rhythm peak align predictably with weight shifts

skill.effect: +30 befriend if the player presses on the sway peak in a rhythm mini-game; stacks with a fruit gift but not with dance.

chains.weakness: Too fast or too loud: sudden loud noises or water splashes trigger a startle reflex, and it withdraws into the sea for 60 s.

journal.en: It has been waiting for a duet.

plausibility.summary: Social duet is a species-typical pair bond retained from mainland founders (F27); the epic is a solitary adult that still performs the obligate ritual and treats any large, slow, low-frequency mimic as a duet partner (heterospecific redirection), not a trait that evolved on an islet with zero conspecifics.
fixes: Social duet is a species-typical pair bond retained from mainland founders (F27); the epic is a solitary adult that still performs the obligate ritual and treats any large, slow, low-frequency mimic as a duet partner (heterospecific redirection), not a trait that evolved on an islet with zero conspecifics.

analogues.organism: African elephant (Loxodonta africana) — low-frequency rumbles and substrate-coupled vibration (Payne et al. 1986, from memory, unverified); sandhill crane pair dances — synchronized slow courtship display.
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

links: pO2 0.34 bar pays for aerobic bulk, so mass is cheap to carry and cheap to drop
At 1.05 g every fall lands heavy: the stomp uses gravity, not muscle
Ground-borne thumps outrange its own eyes in the turbid coastal air

skill.effect: 6 m radius, knocks down creatures under 200 kg for 2 s and cracks rock armour; 3 s recovery between stomps.

chains.weakness: It needs dry footing: lure it into the shallows or onto wet kelp and its own mass sinks and slides, and it cannot stomp while wading.

journal.en: Each step lands like a small landslide.

plausibility.summary: Tie knockdown radius to compact tidal flat or rock; damp sand and wading absorb shock so stomp becomes mainly close-range intimidation (matches weakness on wet kelp). Cap stomp frequency by cardiac/aerobic load despite high pO₂.
fixes: Tie knockdown radius to compact tidal flat or rock; damp sand and wading absorb shock so stomp becomes mainly close-range intimidation (matches weakness on wet kelp). Cap stomp frequency by cardiac/aerobic load despite high pO₂.

analogues.organism: African elephant — footfall-generated seismic signals detected at distance (O'Connell-Rodwell et al., elephant vibration communication, from memory, unverified); cassowary — lethal stomp/kick display.
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

temperament: Slow, deliberate, and socially complex; it moves with the patience of a landscape feature.
moments: A slow, rhythmic sway that harmonizes with a distant Rondo's hum across the water.
The islet's causeway opening at spring low tide, revealing the Coloso's footprints in the wet tuff.
A gentle nudge that clears a path through the giant tree's roots.
